description: Researchers at UC Berkeley have identified a compound that could transform weight-loss treatment by helping the body burn more energy instead of suppressing appetite like Ozempic and Wegovy. In mice, the compound boosted energy expenditure by up to 18%, improved blood sugar control, reduced liver fat, and promoted weight loss without significant muscle loss. Even more promising, combining it with existing GLP-1 medications produced greater benefits than either treatment alone.
title: Experimental compound burns fat without sacrificing muscle

description: A new study has uncovered a surprising concern hiding in popular plant-based foods and drinks. Researchers tested 212 vegan and vegetarian products sold in the UK, including meat alternatives, oat milk, almond milk, and soy milk, and found that every single one contained at least one potentially harmful fungal toxin. Known as mycotoxins, these naturally occurring compounds can contaminate grains, legumes, and seeds during farming and storage.
title: Scientists tested 212 plant-based foods. Every single one contained fungal toxins

description: A bizarre whale that lived roughly 6 million years ago had a face so dramatically crooked that scientists believe it may have been the most asymmetrical of any mammal. Discovered in Peru, the extinct pygmy sperm whale Scaphokogia huachafo had an enormous downward-curving snout and a skull so distorted that researchers initially thought it had been damaged after death. Instead, its strange anatomy appears to have been an extraordinary evolutionary adaptation for hunting along the seafloor.
title: This 6-million-year-old whale may have had the most crooked face in mammal history

description: Scientists have discovered a strange bacterium hiding beneath the skin of deep-sea creatures known as sea pigs, revealing an unexpected biological partnership. The microbe has an unusually tiny genome, yet more than a quarter of its DNA is devoted to making surface proteins, some of them exceptionally large. Researchers suspect it depends heavily on its host for survival, but what the sea pigs gain in return remains a mystery.
title: Something strange is living beneath the skin of deep-sea pigs

description: Hydrogen flames can shift from bright orange to nearly invisible depending on something unexpected: tiny amounts of sodium floating in the air. Scientists say this discovery could help make future hydrogen-powered stoves and ovens safer by replacing visual flame detection with specialized sensors.
title: Why hydrogen flames can glow orange, then turn nearly invisible

description: A surprising new study suggests Antarctica's towering ice cliffs may be less vulnerable to catastrophic collapse than scientists once feared. After tracking more than 15,000 ice cliffs, researchers discovered that even the tallest cliffs, which can collapse at alarming speeds, often stabilize rather than triggering an unstoppable chain reaction. Underwater ridges, surrounding water, and broken ice appear to provide natural defenses against further collapse.
title: Antarctica’s ice cliffs are collapsing faster than expected, but there’s a twist

description: Why do Ozempic and Wegovy produce dramatic weight loss for some people but disappointing results for others? Scientists are investigating whether the body's hidden energy-saving response could help explain the difference and unlock more effective, personalized weight-loss treatments.
title: Why don't weight-loss drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy work for everyone?
